alternate_names: Diguva Ahobilam Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
deities: Prahlada Varada Narasimha — the Lord as boon-giver to Prahlada
Bhargava Narasimha — the form worshipped by Parashurama (Bhargava Rama), under the Karanja tree

history.period: 16th century (Lower temple structure); Bhargava shrine legend ancient
history.summary: This CSV row conflates two distinct shrines of the Nava Narasimha circuit, documented together here: (1) the Prahlada Varada temple, the main accessible temple in the village of Lower (Diguva) Ahobilam, which also houses the festival (utsava) deities of the hill temples; (2) the Bhargava Narasimha shrine about 2 km away, where Parashurama is said to have done penance and witnessed Narasimha tearing Hiranyakashipu — the Lord is worshipped under a Karanja tree (hence Karanja Narasimha) holding the Saaranga bow, with Prahlada at his lotus feet, near Akshaya/Pushkara Tirtha. The Lower Ahobilam temple dates from the Tuluva Vijayanagara period, was sacked with the rest of the complex in 1578, and was restored in the modern era. Coordinates given are for the Diguva temple (from the temple trust's own site); the Bhargava shrine lies ~2 km away and is reached by local jeep/auto through forest terrain.

name: Prahalada Varada / Bhargava Narasimha Temple (Lower Ahobilam)
town_description: Ahobilam is a temple town in Allagadda mandal, Nandyal district, Andhra Pradesh, set in the Nallamala hills of the Eastern Ghats. It is split into Lower (Diguva) Ahobilam, the road-accessible village base, and Upper (Eguva) Ahobilam about 8 km uphill along a ghat road, and is the centre of the Nava Narasimha pilgrimage circuit.

travel.airport: Kurnool Airport (nearest domestic); Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (nearest international)
travel.road: Lower Ahobilam accessible by road (buses from Nandyal/Allagadda); Bhargava shrine approx. 2 km by local jeep/auto; ghat road to Upper Ahobilam approx. 8 km

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (avoid monsoon forest treks)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Lower (Diguva): 6:30 AM-1:00 PM, 3:00-8:00 PM; Bhargava/forest shrines approx. 9:00 AM-4:00 PM, daylight only (some variation across sources)
